data.cultural_impact: The Christian name "Selma" has its roots in Greek mythology, with Selene being the goddess of the moon. This name has been popular in Christian circles, likely due to the connection between the Biblical figure of the Virgin Mary and the moon goddess. In some Christian cultures, Mary is known as the "New Moon" or "Cause of the New Moon," symbolizing her role in bringing new life into the world. The name Selma may also carry associations with the English term "selvage," which in its origin means 'edge of a fabric' or 'defending the boundaries.'
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Selma can represent a strong, radiant, and nurturing female presence. It can be seen as a reminder of Mary's role as a protectress or intercessor, guarding the boundaries of faith and leading her people through the darkest times with her light. The name may also evoke the idea of the moon's cyclical nature, symbolizing the sacred doctrine of eternal life and renewal found in Christianity.
